title: Soft-tenant-quarantine-ttl-to-dampen-surge-noise-and-improve-failover-stability
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduces a non-disruptive tenant soft-quarantine (TTL-based) to dampen request surges, reduces cascading circuit flips, and provides a safe rollout path with metric-backed rollback.
description:
Motivation: During sustained cross-tenant spikes we observed oscillating circuit states and noisy neighbor slowdowns even after capacity throttles engaged. This PR adds a lightweight, time-to-live (TTL) based 'soft quarantine' layer in the routing stack that temporarily attenuates low-priority tenant traffic without an immediate hard eviction. Goals: 1) reduce circuit thrash by avoiding immediate hard cutovers, 2) allow short-lived surge noise to decay rather than escalate to regional failovers, 3) preserve high-priority SLA traffic while making degradation observable and reversible.

What this change does: 
- Introduces a SoftQuarantineManager that tracks per-tenant quarantine epochs with a configurable TTL and decay window.
- Adds a fallthrough router path (attenuated path) that scales request throttling progressively based on tenant priority weight and observed SLO breach score.
- Implements a sticky-circuit hint: when a tenant is moved into soft quarantine, subsequent requests carry a hint so downstream nodes can prefer cached results and avoid repeated cold starts that worsen latency.
- Adds metrics and tracing: quarantine.entered, quarantine.exited, quarantine.ttl_remaining, quarantine_request_ratio, circuit_hint_hit. These are surfaced in Console and used by autoscaling policies.
- Fastpatch behavior for hotfix rollout: feature toggled behind runtime flag 'soft_quarantine.enabled' and 'soft_quarantine.ttl_seconds' with defaults conservative (30s TTL, 3x decay ramp).

Compatibility and safety: The soft quarantine is additive and layered before hard evictions and tenant-throttler gates. It will never drop requests outright; instead it applies progressive token-based acceptance and lower-cost execution paths. It is designed to be disabled at runtime with zero restarts.

Checklist (all items in this single paragraph to keep description contiguous): - [x] design doc referenced (Linear ENG-9821) - [x] unit tests for QuarantineManager TTL logic - [x] integration test for fallthrough router behavior under synthetic surge - [x] telemetry hooks added and dashboards updated - [x] feature flag and safe rollback plan - [x] staged rollout to Dedicated then Hosted regions

Testing and benchmarks: Synthetic replay of a known noisy-tenant incident (SUP-4112) shows 42% reduction in circuit flips over a 10-minute window and 18% improvement in p95 tail for prioritized tenants. Cost impact negligible: slightly higher per-request CPU on attenuated path but fewer expensive failovers overall.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary in one dedicated pool (low-traffic) for 24h with soft_quarantine.enabled=true and TTL=30s. 2) Stage to two regions with TTL ramp to 60s over 48h. 3) Global enable with default TTL 30s and monitoring alarms on quarantine_request_ratio > 0.25 and circuit_flip_rate > baseline + 10%.

Rollback: Toggle soft_quarantine.enabled=false or set TTL=0. Both are instantaneous and will be used automatically if alarm thresholds trigger.

Related work: This complements existing SLO enforcer changes from ENG-9873 and reduces coupling between the throttler and hard eviction code paths.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on QuarantineManager concurrency (lock-free tombstone expiry), the router admission policy heuristics, and the impact on token accounting. Metric names are intentionally short to avoid cardinality blowups.

review_comments: Ethan Liu (reviewer): Can you clarify how TTL expiry interacts with the local cache pruning? I worry about stale tombstones causing prolonged attenuation.

Author (Asha): The manager emits tombstone events to the local cache agent; expiry triggers a tombstone_remove event which allows immediate cache refresh. I've added a unit test to validate tombstone_remove != tombstone_gc to avoid cache stalls.
María Gomez (reviewer): Prefer configurable backoff multiplier per tenant class rather than hardcoded 3x. Also please ensure metric dimensions do not include tenant ID (use priority class only).
Author (Asha): Switched to backoff multiplier surface in runtime flags and removed tenant_id dimension from telemetry. Updated tests and docs.
Owen Patel (reviewer): Observability looks good. Suggest adding alert for quarantine_request_ratio sustained over 200% of baseline for 5m.
Author (Asha): Added alarm to Console dashboard and included thresholds in the rollout section.
ci_summary: All CI checks passed after the second run. First run had a flaky integration test (surge_replay) which was split and stabilized. Linting and static analysis pass. Performance microbenchmarks within acceptable variance.
